title: PraxisMesh partnership discovery — edge & SaaS onramp

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-19 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions), Evan Turner (PraxisMesh Head of Partnerships), Maya Chen (CTO), Luis Ortega (Infra), Asha Rao (Biz Dev)

Summary (auto): quick partner discovery to map integration options for PraxisMesh edge-saas onramp. Focus on private deployment vs hosted, KMS/key rotations, routing and failover, pilot acceptance criteria.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick go-round for intros?
00:08 Evan: yeah thanks jordan, im evan, head of partnerships at praxismesh, we run a gateway that brings customers edge compute + a multi-tenant control plane, maya is our cto, luis runs infra.
00:18 Maya: hi all, excited to learn about redwood's runtime and how a reseller/onramp could look.
00:24 Jordan: perfect. priya, want to intro yourself?
00:27 Priya (Redwood SE): sure, im priya, i'm the se who works on private deploys and performance tuning — latency, batching, kv cache, all the fun bits. samir is our solutions lead who handles partner commercial patterns.
00:40 Samir (Redwood Solutions): hey everyone.
00:42 Luis: cool, thanks. quick ask up front — we're sensitive about data residency and key control, so if we go reseller we need a pattern that gives customers the option of holding keys or us holding them, and audit logs.
00:56 Jordan: noted. that's very common. quick agenda: 1) your constraints and goals 2) integration patterns (hosted api vs dedicated vs private) 3) security/compliance checklist 4) pilot scope and next steps. ok?
01:08 Maya: sounds good.

02:04 Evan: to frame it — praxismesh bundles edge inference into an embeddable SaaS for telco and retail customers. we want to offer redwood as the inference engine inside our control plane for customers that need higher quality LLM features but dont want to re-invent serving. two paths: marketplace/reseller where praxismesh sells redwood-backed inference as a managed add-on, or an on-prem/private joint offering for larger customers.
02:30 Jordan: great. can you describe typical qps / tokens per request distribution? even ballpark is helpful to size dedicated pools.
02:40 Maya: right now our 95th percentile request size is around 450 tokens for the chat-like flows, median is ~120 tokens. QPS burst profile is spiky — campaigns push up 3-4x baseline for 10–30 min windows.
03:00 Priya: spiky bursts — that matters for autoscaling and for our routing policies; we can do burst capacity but need to understand if you have strict latency p95 SLOs. what are you aiming for?
03:12 Luis: customers expect sub-200ms token latency for synchronous features; for async batch jobs they're ok with higher. most sensitive is small prompt completions where latency is visible.
03:24 Priya: okay, that guides kernel selection and batching config. we typically recommend continuous batching with dynamic batch caps for spiky workloads to keep tail latency predictable.

04:15 Evan: commercially, we need to see what margin we can get as a reseller. but before that we need to validate technical fit. can redwood run in our control plane — vpc peering or a private package?
04:28 Jordan: yes. three primary patterns: 1) Hosted Redwood API — fastest to market, we host and you resell with a managed SLA; 2) Redwood Dedicated — reserved capacity pools we can carve for praxismesh customers with stronger isolation; 3) Redwood Private — we ship a customer-controlled control plane that runs in your VPC or on-prem. each has tradeoffs on cost, latency, and control.
04:50 Maya: for telco customers, VPC/on-prem is often required. Do you support hardware isolation and on-prem GPU bundles?
04:58 Priya: yes to both — our private package supports an on-prem runtime and we work with partners for validated GPU fleets. kernel selection and quantization profiles are configurable but we do need some telemetry for performance tuning.
05:12 Evan: telemetry is okay if its pseudonymized, but we need audit logs and explicit key management.
05:18 Jordan: understood. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard APIs. you can opt for customer-managed keys (we never see plaintext) or keys managed by Redwood for convenience — both supported.
05:31 Maya: how does the KV cache behave across tenants? we want cold start penalties low but cant leak state between customers.
05:38 Priya: KV cache is strictly tenant-scoped in private and dedicated patterns; hosted has multi-tenant caching with namespace isolation. cold-start warmers are available as a config — we can pre-warm commonly used prefixes for your telco flows.

06:20 Luis: network topology question — if we run redwood in our VPC, how do upgrades work and what's the blast radius? we need rolling upgrades without downtime.
06:30 Priya: rolling upgrades with canaries are standard, we use canary + automatic fallback to previous model if regression is detected. for private deployments you control maintenance windows, and we provide an ops playbook.
06:44 Evan: regarding compliance, our larger customers ask for SOC2, ISO and audit logs. do you have those?
06:50 Jordan: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, pursuing ISO 27001; we can share the compliance pack and scope matrix.

08:00 Maya: one of our core constraints is bandwidth and connectivity at certain edge POPs. we might need an offline inference mode or proxy cache for low-connectivity sites. how flexible is the runtime?
08:12 Priya: the runtime is GPU-optimized and requires connectivity for model weights and control plane. there is an emerging pattern we support where smaller quantized models are pinned on edge nodes so inference can happen locally with periodic sync. it's more of a hybrid edge/offline model — we'll need to evaluate quantization artifact impact on quality.
08:36 Luis: can you do INT8 or 4-bit quantization? we care about quality.
08:40 Priya: yes, INT8 and 4-bit are supported. we provide quantization profiles and baseline evals so you can understand quality deltas; recommend running A/B evals against your prompt sets.

10:00 Evan: perfect. on the commercial side: for a pilot we want clear unit economics. can we get a JPUs-per-1000-requests cost estimate?
10:12 Samir: we usually model on tokens and GPU hours. for your median token sizes and burst profile we'd propose a pilot with a small dedicated pool and burst capacity, estimate will be sent as a simple spreadsheet.
10:24 Maya: send us the spreadsheet model, we need to map to our pricing.

12:05 Jordan: question — what internal tooling will you use to measure SLA during pilot? do you have existing tracing that can emit per-request IDs?
12:12 Luis: yes we have tracing and can add headers. we'll need guidance on the trace hooks.
12:16 Priya: we'll provide a tracing integration doc and a sample agent.

14:00 Evan: security deep dive — we will require SSO for admin console and RBAC for partner consoles. do you support SAML/ OIDC and SCIM?
14:12 Jordan: yes SAML and OIDC supported; SCIM for provisioning. single-sign on integration is straightforward, and admin RBAC maps to roles you define.
14:25 Maya: audit log retention — we might need 7 years for some telco customers.
14:30 Jordan: long retention is an add-on; we can talk archival policies and log shipping to your SIEM.

16:00 Luis: on model governance, we need controls to pin model versions per customer and to rollback quickly. how does redwood handle model rollouts?
16:10 Priya: rollouts are configurable — canary + percent-based rollouts and automatic fallback on quality regressions. you can pin customers to specific model versions or locked quantized variants.

18:45 Evan: potential pilot success metrics: p95 token latency < 200ms for sync flows, error rate < 0.5% and quality threshold measured by rate of satisfied completions on a prompt set. is that doable?
18:58 Priya: those are reasonable targets depending on model choice; we'll propose model variants and quant profiles and run an AB test during pilot.

21:30 Maya: question on billing and metering — do you expose token-level usage API or only invoices? we want near real-time metrics for internal billing.
21:40 Jordan: we expose token-level usage via our console and can provide an API/webhook for usage events. for dedicated/private we can also provide per-route breakdowns for accounting.

24:00 Evan: integration pattern idea — praxismesh could broker keys and resell redwood in marketplace, or we could co-deliver private bundles. what are the typical partner templates?
24:12 Samir: we have three partner templates: 1) Marketplace reseller (hosted) — simple margin band, we handle infra; 2) Co-managed dedicated — reserved capacity with partner margin and joint support SLAs; 3) Private OEM — you run the control plane and we provide software + support, higher margin to partner. we'll share templates.
24:38 Asha: do you have minimums for OEM/private? some customers expect small-footprint pilot before committing.
24:46 Jordan: pilots can be small — e.g., a single-node private stack for validation — then scale to reserved pools.

28:00 Luis: operational question — how do you handle garbage collection of cached context and potential PII retention?
28:08 Priya: we support retention policies per customer and a purge API. PII scrubbing is a separate pipeline we can run pre-ingest or as a post-process; we'll share guidance.

31:00 Evan: ok next steps then?
31:06 Jordan: recap: redwood will send private deployment checklist, KMS integration spec, compliance pack, and a pilot cost model spreadsheet. praxismesh will send throughput histograms, trace header spec, and confirm infra for pilot. schedule technical kickoff week of 8/31.
31:22 Maya: sounds good.
31:30 Evan: timeline expectations — if pilot starts early sept, a production go-live for select customers could be late q4 depending on pilot results and procurement.
31:40 Jordan: that's reasonable.

35:00 Maya: one more quick technical — if we want to use a GPU partner you already validated, can we use them or do you require specific hardware?
35:08 Priya: we have validated lists but can work with partner hardware as long as it meets drivers and kernel requirements; will require some perf validation.
35:20 Luis: ok we'll inventory potential hardware vendors and share.

40:00 Jordan: i'll note for the pilot we recommend two things: 1) a conserved prompt set for quality evals 2) a baseline traffic replay to validate burst behavior.
40:12 Priya: we'll provide a small harness to replay traffic and to measure p95 and token cost.

45:00 Evan: thanks all — anything else?
45:04 Maya: just to confirm action on security docs exchange.
45:08 Jordan: yes we'll send that first.
45:12 Asha: thanks everyone.

50:00 Meeting end: quick verbal close and confirm calendar invite for kickoff week of 8/31.

Notes about transcript quality: some speaker labels auto-inserted, a few acronyms mis-transcribed (SOC2 -> SO C two), SAML spelled S A M L in places, and occasional dropped filler words.
